An Ouchi retainer who serves as deputy governor of Bungo.
In the Siege of Kagamiyama Castle, he sets out to relieve the castle, which is under attack by the Amago, but does not arrive in time. (Ep. 2)

An Ouchi retainer who serves as deputy governor of Bungo.
In the Siege of Kagamiyama Castle, he sets out to relieve the castle, which is under attack by the Amago, but does not arrive in time. (Ep. 2)
In the Battle of Kanayama Castle, he sets out to take the castle. (Ep. 4)

An Ouchi retainer who serves as deputy governor of Bungo.
In the Siege of Kagamiyama Castle, he sets out to relieve the castle, which is under attack by the Amago, but does not arrive in time. (Ep. 2)
He also takes part in the Battle of Kanayama Castle. (Ep. 4)
In the end, he tries to stop Sue Harukata, who is plotting rebellion, but is killed by a ninja sent by Hironaka Takakane. (Ep. 10)
An Ouchi retainer and lord of Kurakakeyama Castle. He follows Sue Harukata in his rebellion.

en:
An Ouchi retainer and lord of Kurakakeyama Castle. He follows Sue Harukata in his rebellion.
In the Suo-Nagato Offensive, he leaves his castle to face the Mouri Army. (Ep. 13)

en: A consort of Mouri Hiromoto, Motonari's father. After the death of Motonari's birth mother, she becomes Hiromoto's principal wife and raises Motonari in his mother's place. From then on, she is a trusted adviser to Motonari.

A consort of Mouri Hiromoto, Motonari's father. After the death of Motonari's birth mother, she becomes Hiromoto's principal wife and raises Motonari in his mother's place. From then on, she is a trusted adviser to Motonari.
She dies while Motonari is struggling through the retreat from Gassan-Toda Castle. When Motonari at last makes it back to Koriyama, he is overcome with grief. Her last words were "A million hearts as one." (Ep. 8)
An Ouchi retainer. On Ouchi Yoshitaka's orders, he takes Kannabe Castle and becomes its lord.

An Ouchi retainer. On Ouchi Yoshitaka's orders, he takes Kannabe Castle and becomes its lord.
After the failed Ouchi attack on Gassan-Toda Castle, he defects to the Amago side. (Ep. 8)

An Ouchi retainer. On Ouchi Yoshitaka's orders, he takes Kannabe Castle and becomes its lord.
After the failed Ouchi attack on Gassan-Toda Castle, he defects to the Amago side. Together with the Amago's Shinguto, he invades the lands of the Kobayakawa clan, which has just lost its head, and faces the Mouri Army, which rushes to the Kobayakawa's aid.
(Ep. 8)

In the Suo-Nagato Offensive, he intercepts the Mouri Army at Rengeyama Castle.

Leader of the Saika group, Hongan-ji followers from Kii. With a gun in his hands, he has no equal.

Leader of the Saika group, Hongan-ji followers from Kii. With a gun in his hands, he has no equal.
In the Battle of Kizugawaguchi, he faces the Oda Army at Ishiyama Hongan-ji while waiting for provisions from the Mouri Army. (Ep. 22)
Head of a ninja clan that lives in the mountains of Aki. Persuaded by Kuchiba Michiyoshi, he joins the Mouri Army.

en:
Head of a ninja clan that lives in the mountains of Aki. Persuaded by Kuchiba Michiyoshi, he joins the Mouri Army.
From then on, he becomes indispensable to the Mouri for gathering intelligence and carrying out covert schemes.
In the Siege of Kannabe Castle, he persuades Nojiri Motosuke, who has taken the field to protect Kannabe's castle town, to join the Mouri Army. (Ep. 9)
When the Mouri destroy the Ouchi clan at Nagato-Katsuyama Castle, he finds a baby. He names the child Hotaru and raises her as his successor.

Head of a ninja clan that lives in the mountains of Aki. Persuaded by Kuchiba Michiyoshi, he joins the Mouri Army.
From then on, he becomes indispensable to the Mouri for gathering intelligence and carrying out covert schemes.
When the Mouri destroy the Ouchi clan at Nagato-Katsuyama Castle, he finds a baby. He names the child Hotaru and raises her as his successor.

Daughter of Kobayakawa Masahira, head of the main house of the Kobayakawa. She marries Takakage, who is already set to be adopted into a branch family of the Kobayakawa. The Kobayakawa clan, which had been split into a main house and a branch family, is thereby united.

An Otomo retainer. Skilled in strategy, he enjoys the trust of Otomo Sorin.
But at Homanzan Castle, he raises the banner of revolt against the Otomo clan. (Ep. 19)

An Otomo retainer. Skilled in strategy, he enjoys the trust of Otomo Sorin.
But at Homanzan Castle, he raises the banner of revolt against the Otomo clan. As a result, he is pursued by Tachibana Dosetsu and others, and asks the Mouri Army for help. (Ep. 19)
Adopted daughter of Ouchi Yoshitaka; her birth father is Naito Okimori. At Yoshitaka's urging, she becomes the wife of Mouri Takamoto. (Ep. 10)

Adopted daughter of Ouchi Yoshitaka; her birth father is Naito Okimori. At Yoshitaka's urging, she becomes the wife of Mouri Takamoto. (Ep. 10)
After Takamoto's death, she devotes herself to raising Terumoto, the son he left behind.
note: No episode tag in the Japanese for the last paragraph.

en:
Adopted daughter of Ouchi Yoshitaka; her birth father is Naito Okimori. At Yoshitaka's urging, she becomes the wife of Mouri Takamoto. (Ep. 10)
After Takamoto's death, she devotes herself to raising Terumoto, the son he left behind, and later sends him out into the world as head of the clan.
An Oda retainer. A general of great valor, of whom it is said, "Kazumasu in the van, Kazumasu in the rear."

An Oda retainer. A general of great valor, of whom it is said, "Kazumasu in the van, Kazumasu in the rear."
In the Battle of Kizugawaguchi, he faces the Mouri Army as it tries to bring provisions into the Hongan-ji. (Ep. 22)

An Oda retainer. A general of great valor, of whom it is said, "Kazumasu in the van, Kazumasu in the rear."
In the Battle of Kizugawaguchi, he faces the Mouri Army as it tries to bring provisions into the Hongan-ji. (Ep. 22)
Then, in the Pacification of Mino and Owari, he leads the vanguard of Oda Nobukatsu's army and clashes with the Mouri Army once again.
(Ep. 26)
Son of Takeda Motoshige and younger brother of Takeda Mitsukazu. He assists his brother at Kanayama Castle.

Son of Takeda Motoshige and younger brother of Takeda Mitsukazu. He assists his brother at Kanayama Castle.
When Mitsukazu is slain by the Mouri Army, Nobushige succeeds him as lord of Kanayama Castle. (Ep. 6)

Son of Takeda Motoshige and younger brother of Takeda Mitsukazu. He assists his brother at Kanayama Castle.
When Mitsukazu is slain by the Mouri Army, Nobushige succeeds him as lord of Kanayama Castle. (Ep. 6)
He joins the Amago Army's invasion of Yoshida-Koriyama Castle, but is driven back by the Mouri and Otomo armies. Kanayama Castle is then attacked and falls. Entrusting his son Takewakamaru to Ankoku-ji, he takes his own life. With this, the Aki-Takeda clan comes to an end. (Ep. 7)
Son of Takeda Motoshige. After his father dies in battle against the Mouri Army, he succeeds to the headship of the Takeda clan and becomes lord of Kanayama Castle.

Son of Takeda Motoshige. After his father dies in battle against the Mouri Army, he succeeds to the headship of the Takeda clan and becomes lord of Kanayama Castle.
When the Ouchi Army besieges his castle, he asks the Amago for reinforcements. (Ep. 4)

Son of Takeda Motoshige. After his father dies in battle against the Mouri Army, he succeeds to the headship of the Takeda clan and becomes lord of Kanayama Castle.
When the Ouchi Army besieges his castle, he asks the Amago for reinforcements. The Mouri Army marches out under Amago command, and thanks to its efforts the Ouchi Army withdraws and he is saved from his plight. (Ep. 4)

Son of Takeda Motoshige. After his father dies in battle against the Mouri Army, he succeeds to the headship of the Takeda clan and becomes lord of Kanayama Castle.
When the Ouchi Army besieges his castle, he asks the Amago for reinforcements. The Mouri Army marches out under Amago command, and thanks to its efforts the Ouchi Army withdraws and he is saved from his plight. (Ep. 4)
But when the Mouri defect from the Amago to the Ouchi, he turns against the Mouri once again. (Ep. 5)

Son of Takeda Motoshige. After his father dies in battle against the Mouri Army, he succeeds to the headship of the Takeda clan and becomes lord of Kanayama Castle.
When the Ouchi Army besieges his castle, he asks the Amago for reinforcements. The Mouri Army marches out under Amago command, and thanks to its efforts the Ouchi Army withdraws and he is saved from his plight. (Ep. 4)
But when the Mouri defect from the Amago to the Ouchi, he turns against the Mouri once again. In the end, he is slain by the Mouri Army in the Pacification of Aki. (Ep. 5)
Military governor of Aki, based at Kanayama Castle. He serves the Ouchi clan, but the Amago's scheming wins him over and he defects.

Military governor of Aki, based at Kanayama Castle. He serves the Ouchi clan, but the Amago's scheming wins him over and he defects.
When Mouri Okimoto, head of the Mouri clan, dies of illness, Motoshige seizes the chance to attack Arita Castle in Kikkawa territory together with his vassals Kumagai Motonao, Kagawa Mitsukage and Koi Naoyuki. (Ep. 1)

Military governor of Aki, based at Kanayama Castle. He serves the Ouchi clan, but the Amago's scheming wins him over and he defects.
When Mouri Okimoto, head of the Mouri clan, dies of illness, Motoshige seizes the chance to advance on Arita Castle in Kikkawa territory together with his vassals Kumagai Motonao, Kagawa Mitsukage and Koi Naoyuki. But he meets a pitiful end, slain by the Mouri Army as it rushes to relieve the castle. (Ep. 1)

An Otomo retainer. From a cadet branch of the Otomo, he is one of the most powerful men in the clan. But in concert with Takahashi Akitane, he raises a rebellion at Tachibana Castle.
(Ep. 19)

An Otomo retainer. From a cadet branch of the Otomo, he is one of the most powerful men in the clan.
In concert with Takahashi Akitane, he raises a rebellion at Tachibana Castle, but is slain by Tachibana Dosetsu. (Ep. 19)
An Otomo retainer. A fierce general, feared by friend and foe alike as "the Thunder God incarnate."

An Otomo retainer. A fierce general, feared by friend and foe alike as "the Thunder God incarnate."
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he leads the Otomo reinforcements against the Mouri Army as it marches to take Moji Castle. (Ep. 14)

An Otomo retainer. A fierce general, feared by friend and foe alike as "the Thunder God incarnate."
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he leads the Otomo reinforcements against the Mouri Army as it marches to take Moji Castle. (Ep. 14)
When Tachibana Akitoshi rebels, Dosetsu leads a punitive force and takes Tachibana Castle.
(Ep. 19)

An Otomo retainer. A fierce general, feared by friend and foe alike as "the Thunder God incarnate."
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he leads the Otomo reinforcements against the Mouri Army as it marches to take Moji Castle. (Ep. 14)
When Tachibana Akitoshi rebels, Dosetsu leads a punitive force and takes Tachibana Castle. Then he faces the Mouri Army once again as it marches to relieve Takahashi Akitane and Akizuki Tanezane. (Ep. 19)

An Otomo retainer. A fierce general, feared by friend and foe alike as "the Thunder God incarnate."
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he leads the Otomo reinforcements against the Mouri Army as it marches to take Moji Castle. (Ep. 14)
When Tachibana Akitoshi rebels, Dosetsu leads a punitive force and takes Tachibana Castle. Then he faces the Mouri Army once again as it marches to relieve Takahashi Akitane. (Ep. 19)
An Amago retainer who serves as one of the clan's middle elders.

An Amago retainer who serves as one of the clan's middle elders.
He introduces his nephew, Yamanaka Shikanosuke, to Amago Yoshihisa. (Ep. 16)

An Amago retainer who serves as one of the clan's middle elders.
He introduces his nephew, Yamanaka Shikanosuke, to Amago Yoshihisa. (Ep. 16)
In the Siege of Gassan-Toda Castle, he stands against the Mouri Army. But he is outmatched, and the castle falls. Hisatsuna is allowed to escape. (Ep. 17)

An Amago retainer who serves as one of the clan's middle elders.
He introduces his nephew, Yamanaka Shikanosuke, to Amago Yoshihisa. (Ep. 16)
In the Siege of Gassan-Toda Castle, he stands against the Mouri Army. But he is outmatched, and the castle falls. Hisatsuna is allowed to escape. (Ep. 17)
Even after the fall of the Amago, he works with Yamanaka Shikanosuke to restore the clan.

In the Siege of Gassan-Toda Castle, he stands against the Mouri Army. But he is outmatched, and the castle falls. Hisatsuna is allowed to escape. (Ep. 17)
Even after the fall of the Amago, he works with Yamanaka Shikanosuke to restore the clan.
In the Battle of Kozuki Castle, he leaves the castle to fight back against the Mouri Army. (Ep. 23)
An Otomo retainer who enjoys Otomo Sorin's trust as a close aide.

An Otomo retainer who enjoys Otomo Sorin's trust as a close aide.
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he defends Moji Castle with Tawara Chikahiro and meets the Mouri Army's attack. (Ep. 14)
An Otomo retainer, credited above all with the campaigns in Buzen.

An Otomo retainer, credited above all with the campaigns in Buzen.
In the Struggle for Moji Castle, he defends Moji Castle with Tawara Chikakata and meets the Mouri Army's attack. (Ep. 14)

Leads a light supply unit. At the Sakurao market, Chosuke swindles Motonari out of money no fewer than three times. But when the deed comes to light, he repents, and at Motonari's urging he joins the Mouri Army.

Leads a heavy supply unit. At the Sakurao market, Chosuke swindles Motonari out of money no fewer than three times. But when the deed comes to light, he repents, and at Motonari's urging he joins the Mouri Army.
A Fife & Drum musician. Once a traveling entertainer, he is attacked by pirates while sailing to Harima. Held captive, he is rescued by the Mouri Army and from then on serves with it. (Ep. 18)
A Military Band musician. Once a traveling entertainer, he is attacked by pirates while sailing to Harima. Held captive, he is rescued by the Mouri Army and from then on serves with it. (Ep. 18)

The lord of Yamato, based at Yamato-Koriyama Castle.
In the Kinai Offensive, he arrives to reinforce the Akechi side and faces the Mouri Army. (Ep. 25)

A daimyo of Mikawa. His childhood name is Takechiyo. He spends most of his boyhood as a hostage.
When Oda Nobunaga slays Imagawa Yoshimoto at the Battle of Okehazama, Ieyasu seizes the chance to gain his independence and becomes an ally of the Oda clan. (Ep. 15)

A daimyo of Mikawa. His childhood name is Takechiyo. He spends most of his boyhood as a hostage.
When Oda Nobunaga slays Imagawa Yoshimoto at the Battle of Okehazama, Ieyasu seizes the chance to gain his independence and becomes an ally of the Oda clan. (Ep. 15)
To Akechi Mitsuhide, whom Nobunaga has stripped of all his lands, he hints that Mitsuhide is the only one near Nobunaga.
(Ep. 24)

A daimyo of Mikawa. His childhood name is Takechiyo. He spends most of his boyhood as a hostage.
When Oda Nobunaga slays Imagawa Yoshimoto at the Battle of Okehazama, Ieyasu seizes the chance to gain his independence and becomes an ally of the Oda clan. (Ep. 15)
To Akechi Mitsuhide, whom Nobunaga has stripped of all his lands, he hints that Mitsuhide is the only one near Nobunaga, and so steers Mitsuhide into striking down Nobunaga. (Ep. 24)
In the Pacification of Mino and Owari, he orders Honda Tadakatsu and others into battle. He plans to crush the Mouri Army with a joint attack by four armies: his own and those of Oda Nobukatsu, Takigawa Kazumasu and Shibata Katsuie. But the Mouri side learns of it, and the plan fails. (Ep. 26)
And then, at Sekigahara, he meets the Mouri Army in a decisive battle.
A senior Ouchi retainer who serves as deputy governor of Nagato.

A senior Ouchi retainer who serves as deputy governor of Nagato.
Acting on the wishes of Ouchi Yoshioki, he negotiates with the Mouri clan, seeking to bring the Mouri over from the Amago side into the Ouchi fold. (Ep. 5)
An Ouchi retainer and grandson of the senior retainer Naito Okimori. Because Sue Harukata is his brother-in-law, he follows Harukata after the rebellion.

An Ouchi retainer and grandson of the senior retainer Naito Okimori. Because Sue Harukata is his brother-in-law, he follows Harukata after the rebellion.
In the Suo-Nagato Offensive, he faces the Mouri Army at Nagato-Katsuyama Castle with Ouchi Yoshinaga. (Ep. 13)

A local lord of Aki, based at Sakurao Castle and on the Ouchi side.
In the Westward Push through Aki, he is attacked by the Mouri Army and loses Sakurao Castle. (Ep. 11)
An Oda retainer of strict, upright character. He handles supply and the procurement of materials without fail, supporting the Oda Army's rapid rise.

An Oda retainer of strict, upright character. He handles supply and the procurement of materials without fail, supporting the Oda Army's rapid rise.
In the Kinai Offensive, he fights back against the Mouri Army in Settsu, alongside Oda Nobutaka. (Ep. 25)

A genin. A ninja who nonetheless hates war, Motosuke takes the field in the Siege of Kannabe Castle to protect Kannabe's castle town, but is persuaded by Seki Masakiyo to join the Mouri Army. (Ep. 10)

A jonin. A ninja who nonetheless hates war, Motosuke takes the field in the Siege of Kannabe Castle to protect Kannabe's castle town, but is persuaded by Seki Masakiyo to join the Mouri Army. (Ep. 10)

A local lord of Aki under the Ouchi, based at Hogi Castle.
In the Westward Push through Aki, he leaves his castle to fight back against the Mouri Army. (Ep. 11)
A naval commander based on Nomijima, in the service of the Kobayakawa clan.

A naval commander based on Nomijima, in the service of the Kobayakawa clan.
He alerts the Mouri Army to the Amago invasion of Bingo and asks for reinforcements. (Ep. 8)

A naval commander based on Nomijima, in the service of the Kobayakawa clan.
He alerts the Mouri Army to the Amago invasion of Bingo and asks for reinforcements. (Ep. 8)
Kobayakawa Takakage, who was to be adopted into a branch family of the Kobayakawa, inherits the main house instead. As a result, Munekatsu operates alongside the Mouri Army from then on. (Ep. 9)
